standard_text: Use the metric prefixes to convert larger units to smaller units for length, mass, and capacity, and describe the base-ten relationships among metric units

key_big: Bigger unit to smaller unit: multiply.
body_html:
Big unit to small unit: multiply

Metric units are built on 10s. Each prefix tells you the size: kilo means 1000, centi means one hundredth and milli means one thousandth. To change a bigger unit into a smaller unit, multiply. You need more of the small units.

MeasureFacts to know
Length1 km = 1000 m   1 m = 100 cm   1 cm = 10 mm   1 m = 1000 mm
Mass1 kg = 1000 g
Capacity1 L = 1000 mL
Example 1: kilometres to metres

3 km = ☐ m

1 km = 1000 m. Multiply: 3 × 1000 = 3000.

Answer: 3000 m

Example 2: two units

2 kg 80 g = ☐ g

2 kg = 2000 g. Then 2000 + 80 = 2080.

Answer: 2080 g (not 2800 g)

Decimals: move the digits to the left

Multiplying by 10 moves every digit 1 place to the left. Multiplying by 100 moves it 2 places, and multiplying by 1000 moves it 3 places.

Example 3: a decimal in metres

2.5 m = ☐ cm

1 m = 100 cm. Multiply: 2.5 × 100 = 250.

Answer: 250 cm (not 25 cm or 205 cm)

Example 4: a decimal in litres

0.75 L = ☐ mL

1 L = 1000 mL. Multiply: 0.75 × 1000 = 750.

Answer: 750 mL

Choose the unit

Pick the unit that gives an easy number. Use mm or cm for small lengths, m for rooms and rinks, and km for trips. Use g for light things and kg for heavy things. Use mL for a spoon or a cup and L for a bathtub.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3 km = 300 m (multiplying by 100)1 km = 1000 m, so 3 km = 3000 m
7 m = 0.07 cm (moving the digits the wrong way)Bigger unit to smaller unit: multiply. 7 m = 700 cm
2.5 m = 205 cm0.5 m is half a metre, 50 cm. So 2.5 m = 250 cm
2 kg 80 g = 2800 g2000 + 80 = 2080 g. Keep the 0 in the hundreds place

faq.q: What metric conversions do Grade 5 students learn in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 5 students use the metric prefixes to change larger units into smaller ones: km to m, m to cm, cm to mm, kg to g and L to mL, including decimals such as 2.5 m = 250 cm.

faq.q: How do you convert kilometres to metres?
faq.a: Multiply by 1000, because 1 km = 1000 m. So 3 km = 3000 m and 1.5 km = 1500 m.

faq.q: Why do I multiply when I change metres to centimetres?
faq.a: A centimetre is smaller than a metre, so you need more of them: 100 cm fit in every metre. Bigger unit to smaller unit always means multiply.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with metric conversions?
faq.a: Using the wrong number, such as multiplying by 100 for km to m or kg to g when the answer needs × 1000. Learning the prefixes kilo (1000), centi (one hundredth) and milli (one thousandth) helps.

sets.title: Length: km to m, m to cm and cm to mm

items.e: Kilo means 1000, so 1 kilometre = 1000 metres. A kilometre is about a 15-minute walk.
Centi means one hundredth, so 100 centimetres make 1 metre. (1000 is the number of millimetres in a metre.)
Milli means one thousandth. 1 cm has 10 small marks on a ruler, and each one is 1 mm. So 1 cm = 10 mm.
1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 3 × 1000 = 3000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3 km = 3000 m. (300 m multiplies by 100, but 1 km is 1000 m.)
1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 7 × 100 = 700. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 7 m = 700 cm. (0.07 cm divides when it should multiply.)
1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 9 × 10 = 90. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 9 cm = 90 mm. (900 mm multiplies by 100, but 1 cm is only 10 mm.)
1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 12 × 1000 = 12 000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 12 km = 12 000 m. (1200 m multiplies by 100 instead of 1000.)
1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 25 × 100 = 2500. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 25 m = 2500 cm.
1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 40 × 10 = 400. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 40 cm = 400 mm. (4 mm divides when it should multiply.)
Each centimetre has 10 small marks, and each small mark is 1 mm. 6 × 10 = 60, so 6 cm = 60 mm. (600 mm multiplies by 100.)
The eraser ends 7 small marks after 4 cm. 4 cm = 40 mm, and 40 + 7 = 47 mm. (4.7 is the length in centimetres, not millimetres.)

1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 20 × 1000 = 20 000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 20 km = 20 000 m. (2000 m uses × 100. Check: 20 km is 20 groups of 1000 m.)

1 m = 1000 mm. Metres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 1000: 3 × 1000 = 3000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3 m = 3000 mm. (300 is the number of centimetres in 3 m, not millimetres.)
6 m = 600 cm. 600 + 8 = 608 cm. The 0 holds the tens place. (680 cm would be 6 m 80 cm.)
2 km = 2 × 1000 = 2000 m. 2000 + 300 = 2300 m. (500 m uses 2 km = 200 m, and 302 m forgets to convert the kilometres.)
5 km = 5000 m. 5000 + 45 = 5045 m. The 0 keeps the hundreds place empty. (5450 m would be 5 km 450 m.)
1 km = 1000 m. 1000 + 5 = 1005 m. (1500 m would be 1 km 500 m, and 1050 m would be 1 km 50 m.)

items.q: Which is the same as 3500 m?

sets.title: Mass and capacity: kg to g and L to mL

items.e: Kilo means 1000, so 1 kilogram = 1000 grams. A 1 kg bag of flour is as heavy as 1000 paper clips.
Milli means one thousandth, so 1000 millilitres make 1 litre. Four 250 mL glasses fill a 1 L jug.
1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 4 × 1000 = 4000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 4 kg = 4000 g. (400 g multiplies by 100, but 1 kg is 1000 g.)
1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 6 × 1000 = 6000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 6 L = 6000 mL. (600 mL uses × 100. A litre has 1000 millilitres.)
1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 9 × 1000 = 9000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 9 kg = 9000 g.
1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 2 × 1000 = 2000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2 L = 2000 mL.
1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 15 × 1000 = 15 000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 15 kg = 15 000 g. (1500 g multiplies by 100 instead of 1000.)
1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 10 × 1000 = 10 000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 10 L = 10 000 mL. Multiplying by 1000 puts 3 zeros after 10.
1 L = 1000 mL. 1000 + 500 = 1500 mL. (600 mL uses 1 L = 100 mL, and 1005 mL would be 1 L 5 mL.)
2 kg = 2000 g. 2000 + 80 = 2080 g. The 0 holds the hundreds place. (2800 g would be 2 kg 800 g.)
4 L = 4000 mL. 4000 + 5 = 4005 mL. (4500 mL would be 4 L 500 mL, and 4050 mL would be 4 L 50 mL.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of apples in kilograms. What is the mass in grams?
items.e: The needle points to 2 kg. 1 kg = 1000 g, so 2 × 1000 = 2000 g. (200 g uses × 100.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a pumpkin. What is the mass in grams?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 2 equal spaces, so each mark is half a kilogram, 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 3 kg: 3000 + 500 = 3500 g. (3050 g reads the half mark as 50 g.)

items.q: The jug is marked in litres. How much water is in it, in millilitres?
items.e: The water is at 2 L. 1 L = 1000 mL, so 2 × 1000 = 2000 mL. (200 mL uses × 100.)

items.q: The jug is marked in litres. How much water is in it, in millilitres?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 equal spaces, so each line is 1000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 2 lines above 1 L: 1000 + 250 + 250 = 1500 mL. (1200 mL counts each line as 100 mL.)

items.q: Find the missing number. 7000 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g, so count the thousands: 7000 g is 7 groups of 1000 g, which is 7 kg. (70 kg uses 1 kg = 100 g.)

items.q: Find the missing number. 8000 mL = ☐ L
items.e: 1 L = 1000 mL. 8000 mL is 8 groups of 1000 mL, which is 8 L. (8000 L forgets to change the unit.)

1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 2.5 × 100 = 250. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 2.5 m = 250 cm. (205 cm reads 2.5 m as 2 m 5 cm, but 0.5 m is half a metre, 50 cm.)

1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 1.5 × 1000 = 1500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.5 km = 1500 m. (150 m multiplies by 100, and 1005 m reads 1.5 km as 1 km 5 m.)

1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 3.5 × 1000 = 3500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3.5 kg = 3500 g. (0.5 kg is half a kilogram, 500 g, so it is not 3005 g.)
1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 0.5 × 1000 = 500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.5 L = 500 mL. Half a litre is 500 mL.
1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 4.5 × 10 = 45. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 4.5 cm = 45 mm. (0.45 mm moves the digits the wrong way.)

1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1.25 × 100 = 125. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1.25 m = 125 cm. (12.5 cm multiplies by 10, and 1250 cm multiplies by 1000.)
1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 2.75 × 1000 = 2750. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.75 L = 2750 mL. (275 mL multiplies by 100, but 1 L is 1000 mL.)

1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 0.75 × 1000 = 750. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.75 kg = 750 g. (75 g uses × 100. A quarter of a kilogram is 250 g, so 0.75 kg is 3 × 250 = 750 g.)
1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 6.4 × 1000 = 6400. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 6.4 km = 6400 m.

1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 0.3 × 100 = 30. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 0.3 m = 30 cm. (3 cm multiplies by 10, and 0.03 cm moves the digits the wrong way.)
1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 7.2 × 10 = 72. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 7.2 cm = 72 mm.

1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 0.25 × 1000 = 250. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.25 L = 250 mL. Check: 0.25 L is a quarter of a litre, and 1000 ÷ 4 = 250.

1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1.05 × 100 = 105. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1.05 m = 105 cm. (150 cm would be 1.5 m. The 0 in 1.05 means 0 tenths.)
1 kg = 1000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1000: 4.08 × 1000 = 4080. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 4.08 kg = 4080 g. (4800 g would be 4.8 kg. Keep the 0 in its place.)
1 L = 1000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1000: 9.6 × 1000 = 9600. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 9.6 L = 9600 mL.
1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 3.02 × 1000 = 3020. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3.02 km = 3020 m. (3200 m would be 3.2 km.)

items.q: Which is the same as 2.4 m?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 2.4 × 100 = 240 cm. (2 m 4 cm is 204 cm. The 4 in 2.4 is 4 tenths of a metre, which is 40 cm.)

items.q: Which is the same as 1.6 kg?
items.e: 0.6 kg = 0.6 × 1000 = 600 g. So 1.6 kg = 1 kg 600 g = 1600 g. (1 kg 6 g reads the decimal digit as grams.)

items.q: The jug is marked in litres. How much juice is in it, in millilitres?
items.e: Each line is half a litre. The juice is 1 line above 2 L, so it is 2.5 L. 2.5 × 1000 = 2500 mL. (250 mL multiplies by 100.)
1 km = 1000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1000: 3.25 × 1000 = 3250. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3.25 km = 3250 m. (3025 m would be 3 km 25 m, which is 3.025 km.)

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a pencil?
items.e: A pencil is about 15 cm long, so centimetres fit. Litres measure capacity and kilograms measure mass.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the distance from Toronto to Ottawa?
items.e: Toronto to Ottawa is a long drive, so kilometres fit. Centimetres and millimetres are far too small.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a full backpack?
items.e: A full backpack is heavy, so kilograms fit. Grams are for light things like a pencil.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a paper clip?
items.e: A paper clip is very light, about 1 g, so grams fit.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much water a bathtub holds?
items.e: A bathtub holds a lot of water, so litres fit. Millilitres are for small amounts, like a spoonful.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much medicine fits in a spoon?
items.e: A spoon holds only a small amount, about 5 mL, so millilitres fit.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the length of a canoe?
items.e: A canoe is about as long as 3 adults lying end to end, so about 5 m. 50 m is half a soccer field.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the mass of a hockey puck?
items.e: A hockey puck fits in your hand and is light, so grams fit. 17 kg is about the mass of a small dog.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for how much a juice box holds?
items.e: A juice box holds much less than a litre, so 200 mL fits. 2 L is a big carton.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the height of a classroom door?
items.e: A door is a little taller than an adult, so about 2 m. 20 m is about as tall as a 6-storey building.

items.q: A metre is ☐ times as long as a centimetre. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 100 cm = 1 m, so a metre is 100 times as long as a centimetre. (10 is for centimetres and millimetres. 0.01 compares the other way.)

items.q: A kilometre is ☐ times as long as a metre. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Kilo means 1000. 1000 m = 1 km, so a kilometre is 1000 times as long as a metre. (100 is for metres and centimetres.)

items.q: The chart shows how to change between length units. What number goes where the ? is?
items.e: The ? is between metres and centimetres. 1 m = 100 cm, so you multiply by 100 to go from m to cm, and divide by 100 to go back.
Change them all to metres: 3 km = 3000 m and 2 km 990 m = 2990 m. 3000 m is the longest. (2900 has the biggest number, but metres are a smaller unit.)
Change them all to grams: 4 kg = 4000 g and 3 kg 950 g = 3950 g. 4000 g is the heaviest.
Change them all to millimetres: 9 cm = 90 mm, 10 cm = 100 mm and 1 m = 1000 mm. 85 mm is the shortest. (85 is the biggest number, but millimetres are the smallest unit.)
1 L = 1000 mL, so 750 mL is less than 1 L. The other amounts are all 1000 mL or more. (750 is a big number, but millilitres are a small unit.)
1 kg = 1000 g, so 2.5 × 1000 = 2500 g. (250 g multiplies by 100, and 2005 g reads 0.5 kg as 5 g.)
Do it in two steps. 1 km = 1000 m, and each metre is 100 cm. 1000 × 100 = 100 000 cm. (1000 cm stops after the first step.)

items.q: Kai says 6 m = 60 cm. What mistake did he make?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 6 m = 6 × 100 = 600 cm. Kai used 10, which is the number of millimetres in a centimetre.

sets.title: Word problems: Terry Fox Run, maple syrup and canoe trips

items.q: Olivia’s school runs the Terry Fox Run. The route is 5 km long. How many metres is that?
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m, so 5 × 1000 = 5000 m. (500 m multiplies by 100.)

items.q: Maya’s backpack has a mass of 4 kg. Her lunch has a mass of 600 g. What is the total mass in grams?
items.e: Change to one unit first: 4 kg = 4000 g. 4000 + 600 = 4600 g. (604 g adds 4 + 600 without converting, and 1000 g uses 4 kg = 400 g.)

items.q: A 2 L carton of milk is poured into glasses that hold 250 mL each. How many glasses can be filled?
items.e: 2 L = 2000 mL. 2000 ÷ 250 = 8 glasses. Check: 4 glasses make 1 L. (500 multiplies 2 × 250, and 125 divides 250 by 2.)

items.q: Emma has 2 m of ribbon. She cuts it into pieces that are 20 cm long. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: 2 m = 200 cm. 200 ÷ 20 = 10 pieces. (1 piece uses 2 m = 20 cm, and 40 multiplies 2 × 20.)

items.q: A portage on a canoe trip is 1.2 km long. How many metres is the portage?
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m, so 1.2 × 1000 = 1200 m. (120 m multiplies by 100, and 1002 m reads 1.2 km as 1 km 2 m.)

items.q: A sugar shack has 5 L of maple syrup. It fills bottles that hold 250 mL each. How many bottles can it fill?
items.e: 5 L = 5000 mL. 5000 ÷ 250 = 20 bottles. Check: 4 bottles make 1 L, and 5 × 4 = 20. (2 bottles uses 5 L = 500 mL, and 4 is the number of bottles in just 1 L.)

items.q: A newborn moose calf has a mass of about 15 kg. About how many grams is that?
Four friends each bring a 750 mL water bottle on a field trip. How many litres of water is that altogether?
items.e: 4 × 750 = 3000 mL. 1 L = 1000 mL, so 3000 mL = 3 L. (3000 L forgets to change the unit, and 30 L uses 1 L = 100 mL.)

items.q: Zoe is 1.35 m tall. How tall is she in centimetres?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 1.35 × 100 = 135 cm. (13.5 cm multiplies by 10, and 1350 cm by 1000.)

items.q: A pumpkin from a farm stand has a mass of 4.25 kg. What is its mass in grams?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g, so 4.25 × 1000 = 4250 g. (425 g multiplies by 100, and 4025 g reads 0.25 kg as 25 g.)

items.q: Noah’s hockey stick is 1.5 m long. His little sister’s stick is 95 cm long. How much longer is Noah’s stick, in centimetres?
items.e: 1.5 m = 150 cm. 150 − 95 = 55 cm. (93.5 cm takes 1.5 from 95 without converting, 80 cm uses 1.5 m = 15 cm, and 10 cm uses 1.5 m = 105 cm.)

items.q: After a snowstorm in Ottawa, there is 0.4 m of snow on the ground. How deep is the snow in centimetres?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 0.4 × 100 = 40 cm. (4 cm multiplies by 10, 400 cm by 1000, and 0.04 cm divides.)

items.q: Arjun runs 3 laps of a 400 m track. Then he runs 2 km more. How many metres does he run in all?
items.e: 3 × 400 = 1200 m. 2 km = 2000 m. 1200 + 2000 = 3200 m. (1400 m uses 2 km = 200 m, 1220 m uses 2 km = 20 m, and 1202 m forgets to convert the 2 km.)

items.q: A bag has 2 kg of flour. Liam uses 750 g to make bread. How much flour is left, in grams?
items.e: 2 kg = 2000 g. 2000 − 750 = 1250 g. (748 g takes 2 from 750 without converting, 1350 g is a regrouping mistake, and 2750 g adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: Kai swims 1 km in a pool that is 25 m long. How many lengths of the pool does he swim?
items.e: 1 km = 1000 m. 1000 ÷ 25 = 40 lengths. Check: 40 × 25 = 1000. (4 lengths uses 1 km = 100 m, and 400 lengths uses 1 km = 10 000 m.)

items.q: A bucket for maple sap holds 8 L. It has 3500 mL of sap in it now. How many more millilitres will fill it?
items.e: 8 L = 8000 mL. 8000 − 3500 = 4500 mL. (3492 mL takes 8 from 3500 without converting, and 11 500 mL adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: The CN Tower in Toronto is 553 m tall. How tall is it in centimetres?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so 553 × 100 = 55 300 cm. (5530 cm multiplies by 10, 553 000 cm by 1000, and 5.53 cm divides by 100.)

items.q: A 1 kg bag of trail mix is shared equally into 8 small bags for a hike. How many grams go in each bag?
items.e: 1 kg = 1000 g. 1000 ÷ 8 = 125 g. Check: 8 × 125 = 1000. (12.5 g uses 1 kg = 100 g, 8000 g multiplies, and 992 g takes away 8.)

items.q: A cross-country ski trail is 3 km 250 m long. Hana skis the trail twice. How many metres does she ski?
items.e: 3 km 250 m = 3000 + 250 = 3250 m. 2 × 3250 = 6500 m. (6050 m uses 3 km 250 m = 3025 m, and 3250 m is only one time around.)

items.q: For Thanksgiving, Ava’s family buys a 7.5 kg turkey and 2 kg 400 g of potatoes. What is the total mass in grams?
